title: qBittorrent
descript: qBittorrent is a BitTorrent client with a clean web UI: add magnet links or .torrent files, queue and seed, set speed limits, search and RSS. It runs as a non-root container, keeps settings and resume data in the app data folder, and writes downloads to a folder you control. The first start generates a random WebUI password in config/qBittorrent/webui-credentials.txt (0600). There is no account or telemetry, but the trackers, DHT nodes and peers of the torrents you add see your public IP.
release_note: 5.3.0-3 rectifies the review findings. F10: the container log no longer contains a plaintext WebUI password. Each installation generates a random password, stores the PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 hash in qBittorrent.conf and keeps the plaintext only in config/qBittorrent/webui-credentials.txt (0600). Change it after the first login and delete the file. F2/F8: the wrapper now seeds the image's /defaults/qBittorrent.conf instead of writing a minimal config, so Downloads\SavePath is /downloads/ and UPnP is off. 5.3.0-2 fell back to /config/Downloads, which this update migrates. F3: stop_grace_period 30s. F7: HostHeaderValidation is disabled before start so the WebUI loads through 8041 and reverse proxies, while login and CSRF protection stay enabled. F11/F4: the README documents the data folders and the deletion steps. F9: restart policy and healthcheck re-verified. S11: umask 077, config and credentials 0600, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges and a uid-1000 tmpfs /run. C2: the licence is corrected to GPL-3.0-or-later for the binary (GPL-2.0-or-later source) and NOTICE is rewritten. C8: the third-party table lists every endpoint, what it sends and how to disable it, including tracker, DHT and peer public-IP exposure, the DB-IP download and the optional STUN, search and RSS endpoints. C10: the README now has repository layout, privacy, notices, build, data and uninstall sections. T1: the image moves to the 2026-11-23 build (5.3.0_v2.1.3-ls489, index digest a8083a33...). V7: deterministic rebuild and the platform file_hash is checked against the local SHA-256.
important: Requires DockerEngine. Log in as admin with the random password in DockerAppData/qbittorrentdocker/config/qBittorrent/webui-credentials.txt (0600), change it and delete the file. Downloads: DockerAppData/qbittorrentdocker/downloads, settings: .../config. Only the WebUI port is published, so incoming peers are limited. Your public IP is visible to the trackers, DHT nodes and peers of every torrent you add, and no VPN is included. Plain HTTP. Use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it.

data_notes: `config/qBittorrent/qBittorrent.conf` keeps every setting, including the PBKDF2 hash of the WebUI password. `config/qBittorrent/webui-credentials.txt` holds the initial random password in plain text (mode 0600) until you change it and delete the file. `config/qBittorrent/BT_backup/` keeps the .torrent metadata and resume data of your torrents, `config/qBittorrent/GeoDB/` the optional DB-IP country database and `config/qBittorrent/logs/` the local application log. `/downloads` receives the payload, with `incomplete/` while a download is running.
design_notes: **Non-root with all capabilities dropped.** uid/gid 1000, `cap_drop: [ALL]` and `no-new-privileges`; `/run` is a uid-1000 tmpfs because s6-overlay needs it before it starts, then the app runs without capabilities.

**First start seeds the image defaults.** `/defaults/qBittorrent.conf` is copied to the config volume, so `Downloads\SavePath=/downloads/`, `TempPath=/downloads/incomplete/` and `Connection\UPnP=false` are active. The minimal config written by 5.3.0-2 silently changed the save path to `/config/Downloads` and turned UPnP back on.

**Random per-install WebUI password, never in the log.** PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 (100000 iterations, 64-byte key) goes into the config, the plaintext only into `webui-credentials.txt` (0600). qBittorrent's temporary-password log line is no longer produced.

**Host-header validation is off, deliberately.** qBittorrent compares the browser's Host port with its own 8080, so through 8041 or a TLS reverse proxy every request returns 401. Login, CSRF protection and the authentication requirement stay enabled. Keep the UI on the LAN or behind a TLS proxy.
**Fixed image digest, never `:latest`.** Docker Hub only, no `privileged`, no `network_mode: host`, no Docker socket, no `cap_add`.
**One published port.** Only the WebUI 8080 is exposed; the BT listen port stays inside the container, the trade-off for the store's single-port rule.
limitations: The WebUI is plain HTTP. Use a TLS reverse proxy before exposing it to the internet.
The BitTorrent listen port (6881) is not published, so incoming peers are limited and speeds may be lower than a desktop client. UPnP is off by default; a router forward can be added manually.

The trackers, DHT nodes and peers of the torrents you add see your public IP and client port. This is inherent to BitTorrent. No VPN is included; use the proxy/VPN settings or a VPN tunnel if that matters.
Host-header validation is disabled so the WebUI works through 8041 and reverse proxies. Do not publish port 8041 directly to the internet.

The initial password is in `DockerAppData/qbittorrentdocker/config/qBittorrent/webui-credentials.txt` (0600). Read it with the TOS File Manager, SMB or SSH, change it on first login and delete the file.
The downloads folder is not visible in TOS File Manager. Manage the files over SMB or SSH, or add the path to a backup task.
Docker applications cannot be upgraded in place in the App Center. Updating means uninstall and reinstall, which keeps the data folders unless you tick delete data.
The aarch64 package is built from the same multi-architecture image index and passes the official conformance check; the runtime smoke test in this environment runs on x86_64 only.
